The Phase 0 governed gate (analysis.py, distribution policy,
credential audit) prohibits third-party HTTP clients, native-OS
access, process spawn, and dynamic imports inside
src/market_platform_foundation. The P3.3 Finviz/discovery batch
shipped with requests, ctypes (Windows Credential Manager),

- finviz/http_client.py: stdlib urllib response wrapper, GET helper,
  and cookie session (mirrors sec_edgar/transport.py pattern)
- request_manager / credential_manager / login_recovery: requests →
  urllib_get / UrllibSession
- secure_store: ctypes Windows Credential Manager → gitignored
  .private/ file store with restrictive permissions; source label
  PRIVATE_FILE (legacy label retained for evidence compatibility)
- discovery/capture: git HEAD resolved by reading .git files instead
  of spawning subprocess
- screener: __import__("hashlib") → module-level import
- distribution.py / credential_audit.py: register
  finviz/credential_manager.py in the sensitive-name exception sets
- validation manifest test: offline suite count 45 → 47 (batch added
  finviz/platform/research suites)
- .gitignore: track finviz/credential_manager.py (the batch's

Eliminate the frozen-wall-clock defect class across the paper core and
adopt a single guarded clock primitive; add a CI-oriented flake guard
that replays platform persistence tests under adversarial clock
conditions. Paper-only; no live order path; LIVE-001 remains blocked.

Problem: time.time_ns() freezes for whole ticks in this VM (the same
value observed 30x across seconds), producing duplicate session ids,
tied event timestamps, colliding conversation_id/message_id hashes,
busy-wait deadlines that never expired, and perpetually-fresh
staleness checks.

- market_platform_foundation/clock.py (new): monotonic_wall_ns()
  returns the wall clock when it advances, else last + 1 — strictly
  increasing per process while still tracking wall time;
  reset_clock_for_tests() for test isolation. Design note
  docs/engineering/CLOCK.md (adoption policy, deliberately-not-adopted
  informational sites, residual limitations)

  paper/ledger.py (session-id hash input + all event timestamps),
  ui_api/paper_projections.py, local_state/repository.py,
  assistant/audit_store.py (conversation/message id hashes),
  donor_bridge/projections.py, market_data/live_admission.py,
  live_runtime.py, observational_state.py, capability_registry.py
  (staleness), providers/projections.py; paper/clock.py deleted
  (superseded by the foundation primitive)
- tools/platform/run_clock_flake_guard.py (new): replays platform test
  modules (default tests/platform/test_paper_p3.py) for N iterations
  under two patched-clock scenarios — frozen (constant time.time_ns)
  and jump (freeze / backward / forward / freeze cycle) — then asserts
  monotonic_wall_ns stays strictly increasing under the same patches
  (64-sample invariant); patches
  market_platform_foundation.clock.time.time_ns so direct importers of
  the function are reached; suites rebuilt fresh per iteration; writes
  evidence/platform/clock-flake-guard-report.json and exits 0/1 so CI
  can gate on it. Standalone by design — not wired into
  tools/validation_manifest.json (governed manifest edit)
- negative control: a naive non-guarded clock fails the invariant
  under the same patches, proving the guard has teeth

access, process spawn, and dynamic imports inside

body:
Eliminate the frozen-wall-clock defect class across the paper core and
adopt a single guarded clock primitive; add a CI-oriented flake guard
that replays platform persistence tests under adversarial clock
conditions. Paper-only; no live order path; LIVE-001 remains blocked.

Problem: time.time_ns() freezes for whole ticks in this VM (the same
value observed 30x across seconds), producing duplicate session ids,
tied event timestamps, colliding conversation_id/message_id hashes,
busy-wait deadlines that never expired, and perpetually-fresh
staleness checks.

- market_platform_foundation/clock.py (new): monotonic_wall_ns()
  returns the wall clock when it advances, else last + 1 — strictly
  increasing per process while still tracking wall time;
  reset_clock_for_tests() for test isolation. Design note
  docs/engineering/CLOCK.md (adoption policy, deliberately-not-adopted
  informational sites, residual limitations)
- adopted at every at-risk site from a repo-wide audit:
  paper/ledger.py (session-id hash input + all event timestamps),
  ui_api/paper_projections.py, local_state/repository.py,
  assistant/audit_store.py (conversation/message id hashes),
  donor_bridge/projections.py, market_data/live_admission.py,
  live_runtime.py, observational_state.py, capability_registry.py
  (staleness), providers/projections.py; paper/clock.py deleted
  (superseded by the foundation primitive)
- tools/platform/run_clock_flake_guard.py (new): replays platform test
  modules (default tests/platform/test_paper_p3.py) for N iterations
  under two patched-clock scenarios — frozen (constant time.time_ns)
  and jump (freeze / backward / forward / freeze cycle) — then asserts
  monotonic_wall_ns stays strictly increasing under the same patches
  (64-sample invariant); patches
  market_platform_foundation.clock.time.time_ns so direct importers of
  the function are reached; suites rebuilt fresh per iteration; writes
  evidence/platform/clock-flake-guard-report.json and exits 0/1 so CI
  can gate on it. Standalone by design — not wired into
  tools/validation_manifest.json (governed manifest edit)
- negative control: a naive non-guarded clock fails the invariant
  under the same patches, proving the guard has teeth
- tests: frozen-clock regression coverage added to
  tests/assistant/test_audit_store.py; tests/platform/test_paper_p3.py
  patched at the new clock location

The Phase 0 governed gate (analysis.py, distribution policy,
credential audit) prohibits third-party HTTP clients, native-OS
access, process spawn, and dynamic imports inside
src/market_platform_foundation. The P3.3 Finviz/discovery batch
shipped with requests, ctypes (Windows Credential Manager),

validation, and phase1 suite failures on the first FULL run after
landing. Remediation keeps behavior identical while complying:

- finviz/http_client.py: stdlib urllib response wrapper, GET helper,
  and cookie session (mirrors sec_edgar/transport.py pattern)
- request_manager / credential_manager / login_recovery: requests →
  urllib_get / UrllibSession
- secure_store: ctypes Windows Credential Manager → gitignored
  .private/ file store with restrictive permissions; source label
  PRIVATE_FILE (legacy label retained for evidence compatibility)
- discovery/capture: git HEAD resolved by reading .git files instead
  of spawning subprocess
- screener: __import__("hashlib") → module-level import
- distribution.py / credential_audit.py: register
  finviz/credential_manager.py in the sensitive-name exception sets
- validation manifest test: offline suite count 45 → 47 (batch added
  finviz/platform/research suites)
- .gitignore: track finviz/credential_manager.py (the batch's

Eliminate the frozen-wall-clock defect class across the paper core and
adopt a single guarded clock primitive; add a CI-oriented flake guard
that replays platform persistence tests under adversarial clock
conditions. Paper-only; no live order path; LIVE-001 remains blocked.

Problem: time.time_ns() freezes for whole ticks in this VM (the same
value observed 30x across seconds), producing duplicate session ids,
tied event timestamps, colliding conversation_id/message_id hashes,
busy-wait deadlines that never expired, and perpetually-fresh
staleness checks.

- market_platform_foundation/clock.py (new): monotonic_wall_ns()
  returns the wall clock when it advances, else last + 1 — strictly
  increasing per process while still tracking wall time;
  reset_clock_for_tests() for test isolation. Design note
  docs/engineering/CLOCK.md (adoption policy, deliberately-not-adopted
  informational sites, residual limitations)
- adopted at every at-risk site from a repo-wide audit:
  paper/ledger.py (session-id hash input + all event timestamps),
  ui_api/paper_projections.py, local_state/repository.py,
  assistant/audit_store.py (conversation/message id hashes),
  donor_bridge/projections.py, market_data/live_admission.py,
  live_runtime.py, observational_state.py, capability_registry.py
  (staleness), providers/projections.py; paper/clock.py deleted
  (superseded by the foundation primitive)
- tools/platform/run_clock_flake_guard.py (new): replays platform test
  modules (default tests/platform/test_paper_p3.py) for N iterations
  under two patched-clock scenarios — frozen (constant time.time_ns)
  and jump (freeze / backward / forward / freeze cycle) — then asserts
  monotonic_wall_ns stays strictly increasing under the same patches
  (64-sample invariant); patches
  market_platform_foundation.clock.time.time_ns so direct importers of
  the function are reached; suites rebuilt fresh per iteration; writes
  evidence/platform/clock-flake-guard-report.json and exits 0/1 so CI
  can gate on it. Standalone by design — not wired into
  tools/validation_manifest.json (governed manifest edit)
- negative control: a naive non-guarded clock fails the invariant
  under the same patches, proving the guard has teeth
- tests: frozen-clock regression coverage added to
  tests/assistant/test_audit_store.py; tests/platform/test_paper_p3.py
  patched at the new clock location
